body:
We need to have a tool, that is able to split audio file into samples, and deduplicate them, by subtracting and different positions. So we can reconstruct notes and the whole composition in formats, acceptable by music production software (Garage Band, Reason, Ableton, Frutty Loops and so on).

https://share.google/aimode/V2byVRjw4ImJRJmYe - check the context.

We should also be recognizing the note of samples, so we can reconstruct midi and so on.

To make sure our software works, we need to use public domain audio music compositions, so we are sure we don't violate any copy rights.

For deduplication, universal data model, and data storage we should prefer associative stack from https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/docs/associative-tech-stack.md

We should start with Rust CLI and library, that takes audio file as input and produces its reconstruction decomposed to all parts we can distinctly separate. And in any popular music (closed + open) formats, so we can use them to reconstruct everything back.

And there also should be a good test, that round trip reconstruction/composition actually works.

comments.body: The requested end state spans lossless audio modeling, sample deduplication, source separation, pitch recognition, MIDI generation, and many production formats. To keep the first prototype reviewable and testable, may I scope this PR to 16-bit PCM WAV input; deterministic deduplication into reusable PCM blocks plus an associative timeline representation; byte-exact WAV reconstruction; monophonic pitch/note detection with Standard MIDI output; and generated/public-domain-safe fixtures—while tracking polyphonic ML source separation and compressed/DAW-native formats as follow-up work?

No, nothing can be separated as follow-up work. No matter how big the task, we do everything here.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
I need actual delivery here, based on all best ideas from all pull requests, and may be even better.
